items.title: Source citations in every episode
items.text: Each line of a script points to the source it came from, and the transcript shows it, so a listener can check any claim. Multi-source episodes already cite every content turn (see CHANGELOG, Unreleased); what remains is showing the citations in the transcript and the episode page.

items.title: Audio and podcast sources
items.text: Drop in an MP3 or a podcast episode as a source: it is transcribed locally (Whisper), punctuation is restored with a word-for-word check, and it is discussed like any other source. A first implementation exists and is in review.

items.title: Saved source trays
items.text: Save a mix of feeds and notes as a template that a watchlist refills on a schedule, so a recurring show needs no clicks.

items.title: Longer, smoother episodes
items.text: Get closer to NotebookLM in length and flow. Measured, not guessed: the public blind test at https://vozonda.com/test/ compares Vozonda, NotebookLM and Open Notebook on the same sources.

items.title: More voice engines, including commercial ones (ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Google, Azure)
items.text: The first wish from a potential user after the launch: more voice engines, including the commercial top models, so a show can sound as good as the best voices available today.

items.title: Vozonda Cloud
items.text: A hosted version, paid per episode with Lightning and without accounts, if enough people ask for it. The waitlist is one anonymous click on https://vozonda.com/#cloud.

items.title: Hosts with a stance
items.text: Give each host a position on a topic, so a debate is a real debate instead of two people agreeing politely.

items.title: Nostr bookmarks as a source
items.text: Bookmark an article in your Nostr app and it becomes an episode, read from your public bookmark list (NIP-51). Not built yet; the About and FAQ pages described it by mistake until #24.
